title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page is titled 'Calculs de cohomologie absolue des Motifs de Tate Z(i)'. On this page Grothendieck guesses what the 'absolute' (motivic) cohomology of Tate motives should be over a finite field and over Spec Z. He starts from the ℓ-adic realization and then extrapolates to integral and rational 'motivic' coefficients. The underlined Q, Z denote motivic coefficient objects.

(1) ℓ-adic computation over a finite field. Let k = F_q, with π = Gal(k̄/k) ≅ Ẑ topologically generated by Frobenius f. For a finitely generated Z_ℓ-module M with continuous π-action:
- H^0 = Ker(1−f),
- H^1 = Coker(1−f) = M/(1−f)M,
- H^i = 0 for i ≥ 2.
For M = Z_ℓ(n), f acts by q^n. Hence:
- H^0(π, Z_ℓ(n)) = 0 for n ≠ 0, and Z_ℓ for n = 0.
- H^1(π, Z_ℓ(n)) ≅ Z_ℓ/(1−q^n), non-canonically. This is Z_ℓ if n = 0. It is 0 if ℓ ∤ 1−q^n, i.e. ω_ℓ(q) ∤ n, where ω_ℓ(q) is the order of q in (Z/ℓ)^*. It is Z/ℓ^{v_ℓ(1−q^n)} otherwise.
Tensoring with Q: H^i(π, Q_ℓ(n)) = 0 for all i when n ≠ 0, and H^0 = H^1 = Q_ℓ when n = 0.

(2) Motivic extrapolation over F_q, with question marks about p-torsion. He crosses out 'H^i(π, Z(n))' and replaces it with 'absolute' cohomology 𝐇^i(F_q, −):
- 𝐇^i(F_q, Q(n)) = 0 for n ≠ 0 and all i.
- 𝐇^0(F_q, Q) = Q and 𝐇^1(F_q, Q) = Q.
- 𝐇^0(F_q, Z) = Z and 𝐇^1(F_q, Z) = Z.
- For n ≠ 0: 𝐇^0(F_q, Z(n)) = 0 and 𝐇^1(F_q, Z(n)) = Z/(1−q^n).
In other words, the absolute theory behaves like cohomology of the discrete Weil group Z = ⟨Frob⟩ acting on a 'lattice' Z(n) on which Frob acts by q^n. It is not like cohomology of the profinite group Ẑ, which would give étale H^1(F_q, Z) = 0 and H^2 = Q/Z.
For n ≥ 1, |𝐇^1(F_q, Z(n))| = q^n − 1. This is the order of Quillen's K_{2n−1}(F_q) (1972), i.e. the later motivic H^1(F_q, Z(n)). It also equals |1/ζ_{F_q}(−n)| — essentially the value of the zeta function at s = −n — though the page does not state this.

(3) Spec Z (below the rule).
- 𝐇^i(Spec Z, Z(1)) = Z for i = 3 and 0 otherwise.
- 𝐇^i(Spec Z, Z) = Z for i = 0 and 0 otherwise.
This is exactly the cohomology of an integral homology 3-sphere. Z(1) plays the orientation/dualizing role, with an integral trace in degree 3 (compare Artin–Verdier, where the degree-3 group is Q/Z for G_m).
Finally he claims that for n ≠ 0 and any Zariski open U ⊂ Spec Z, 𝐇^i(Spec Z, Q(n)) → 𝐇^i(U, Q(n)) is an isomorphism for all i. The next page tests this via purity: i_x^! M = i_x^* M(−1)[−2] gives a localization sequence. He finds the needed condition is n ≠ 1, and for n = 1 obtains the Q^S terms.

Purpose: to calibrate a hoped-for 'absolute cohomology of motives' over finite fields and Spec Z with integral coefficients and arithmetic duality (Spec Z as a 3-dimensional object).
errors: The final excision claim is stated for n ≠ 0, but by purity the boundary terms involve the residue-field cohomology H(F_p, Q(n−1)). With his own values this is nonzero exactly when n = 1, so the correct condition is n ≠ 1. For n = 0 the boundary term is H(F_p, Q(−1)), which vanishes. Grothendieck himself corrects this on the next page ('Si n ≠ 1 ... tout i [est-ce vrai ??]' and the separate n = 1 analysis).

𝐇^i(Spec Z, Z(1)) = 0 for i ≠ 3 ignores torsion: H^1 should contain Z^* = {±1}, as in any motivic or Weil-étale theory. The vanishing is only true modulo 2-torsion, or for a suitably compactified/modified theory (the archimedean place is not treated).

The integral values over F_q (𝐇^1(F_q, Z) = Z, 𝐇^1(F_q, Z(n)) = Z/(1−q^n) for all n ≠ 0, including n < 0) do not match Voevodsky motivic cohomology. There H^1(F_q, Z(0)) = 0 and H^*(F_q, Z(n)) = 0 for n < 0. They also do not match étale cohomology, where H^1 = 0 and H^2 = Q/Z. They do match a Weil-group (Weil-étale-type) theory.

The p-part is left open ('mod p-groupes?'). Z_p(n) has no Galois-module meaning over F_q, so the ℓ-adic table only justifies the prime-to-p part. The true p-part of K_{2n−1}(F_q) is in fact 0, which is consistent with Z/(q^n−1) having no p-torsion.
Minor: for ℓ = 2 the equivalence ℓ | 1−q^n ⇔ ω_ℓ(q) | n holds trivially, since ω_2(q) = 1. The formula is fine but the notation is degenerate there.

ideas.what: Galois cohomology of Ẑ via Ker/Coker(1−F) and the computation of H^*(F_q, Z_ℓ(n)), Q_ℓ(n)
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology of procyclic groups; ℓ-adic Tate twists over finite fields

ideas.what: Integral 'absolute' cohomology of Tate motives over F_q: 𝐇^1(F_q, Z(n)) = Z/(1−q^n), 𝐇^0 = 0 for n ≠ 0, rationally zero
ideas.modern_name: Motivic cohomology of finite fields, equivalently Quillen's K_{2n−1}(F_q) = Z/(q^n−1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen 1972 (K-theory of finite fields); motivic interpretation Beilinson/Lichtenbaum/Voevodsky

ideas.what: 𝐇^0(F_q, Z) = 𝐇^1(F_q, Z) = Z and 𝐇^1(F_q, Q) = Q: absolute cohomology modeled on the discrete Frobenius (Weil group Z) rather than Ẑ
Spec Z has integral absolute cohomology of a homology 3-sphere: H^*(Spec Z, Z) = Z in degree 0, H^*(Spec Z, Z(1)) = Z in degree 3
ideas.modern_name: Integral Artin–Verdier duality / Weil-étale duality; 'Spec Z ~ S^3' in arithmetic topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin–Verdier 1964 (Q/Z version); Mazur (~1963–73, primes as knots); Lichtenbaum, Flach–Morin (integral Weil-étale); Morishita, Kapranov–Reznikov

ideas.what: Invariance of 𝐇^i(−, Q(n)) under shrinking Spec Z for n ≠ 0 (corrected to n ≠ 1 on next page), via purity i^! = i^*(−1)[−2]
ideas.modern_name: Localization sequence for motivic cohomology with rational coefficients; vanishing of H^*(F_p, Q(m)) for m ≠ 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen localization (1973), Levine/Bloch localization for higher Chow groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck postulates an absolute cohomology over F_q in which H^0(F_q, Z) = H^1(F_q, Z) = Z and H^1(F_q, Q) = Q. That is, cohomology of the discrete Frobenius group Z, not of Ẑ. This is precisely the defining feature of Lichtenbaum's Weil-étale cohomology, introduced decades later. Grothendieck's motivic Galois-theory notes are not cited as an antecedent.
missed.quote: 𝐇^0(F_q, Z) = Z (mod p-groupes?), 𝐇^1(F_q, Z) = Z ... 𝐇^1(F_q, Q) = Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that the 'Weil-group' integral structure of absolute motivic cohomology was already in Grothendieck's motivic programme. This is relevant to the history of Weil-étale cohomology and its role in special-value conjectures.

missed.claim: An explicit integral prediction that Spec Z has the absolute cohomology of a homology 3-sphere. Z sits in degree 0 for trivial coefficients, and Z sits in degree 3 for Z(1), as an integral fundamental class. This is an integral refinement of Artin–Verdier (which gives Q/Z) and the motivic form of the 'Spec Z is a 3-manifold' analogy.
missed.quote: 𝐇^i(Spec Z, Z(1)) = { 0 si i ≠ 3 ; Z si i = 3 }
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is essentially the shape later sought in integral Weil-étale duality (Lichtenbaum, Flach–Morin) and in arithmetic topology. If the page dates from 1965, it predates or is contemporaneous with Mazur's published formulations.

missed.claim: Prediction of the integral groups 𝐇^1(F_q, Z(n)) = Z/(1−q^n) with vanishing rational part, a formula later realized by Quillen's computation of K_{2n−1}(F_q). The page's dating (1965–ca. 1977) is uncertain, so priority is unclear.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows Grothendieck's motivic cohomology anticipations. The mathematical content itself is now well known.

deep.surprise_reason: The ℓ-adic part is routine. The integral extrapolations, however, are striking: H^1(F_q, Z) = Z (Weil-group / Weil-étale behaviour) and Spec Z as an integral homology 3-sphere with Z(1) dualizing in degree 3. They foreshadow Lichtenbaum's Weil-étale cohomology and integral Artin–Verdier duality, which are not usually traced to Grothendieck. They are tentative guesses with question marks, and the dating is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: 'f = frob^q' is probably 'f = frob_q' (Frobenius of F_q).
In the right margin the condition reads 'i.e. n ≢ 0 (ω_ℓ(q))', with a crossed-out word beneath.
The crossed-out heading line is 'H^i(π, Z(n))' with an underlined (motivic) Z.
'(id)' in 𝐇^0(F_q, Z(n)) = 0 (id) means 'same caveat (mod p-groups?)'; 'n ≠ 0' is written below the Z(n) arguments.
In the last formula the excision condition is written 'et n ≠ 0 (tout i)'; the next page corrects this to n ≠ 1.
